title: Fundamental groups commute with algebraic constant-field limits
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $L/K$ a separable algebraic extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $K$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For each intermediate field $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$ with $[E:K]<\infty$, put $X_E=X_0\times_K E$, and put $X_L=X_0\times_K L$ [def-pc-base-change]. Assume that $X_L$ and every $X_E$ are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and choose a geometric point $\bar x\to X_L$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Give each $X_E$ the composite point $\bar x_E$. Use the profinite fundamental groups of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. The homomorphisms induced by the projections [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] give an isomorphism of topological groups
$$\pi_1(X_L,\bar x)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{[E:K]<\infty}\pi_1(X_E,\bar x_E).$$
The transition homomorphism for $E\subseteq E'$ is induced by $X_{E'}\to X_E$. The inverse limit means the subgroup of compatible families in the product, with its subspace topology, and the displayed map has components induced by $X_L\to X_E$.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion (fundamental group of a connected qcqs affine-transition inverse limit), specialized to the constant-field system X_E; X_L is its limit because L is the union of its finite intermediate fields.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finite intermediate fields of $L/K$, ordered by inclusion. It is a set since its elements are subsets of $L$, and is nonempty since $K\in I$. The finite-subextension presentation of [lem-kun-algebraic-separable-smooth] makes it directed: any two finite subextensions lie in a finite subextension. Write $G_E=\pi_1(X_E,\bar x_E)$ and $G_L=\pi_1(X_L,\bar x)$. The hypotheses on $K,L,X_0$ are exactly those of [lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent], so its object and morphism descent assertions apply to this system. No normality or Galois hypothesis on $L/K$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: For $Y=X_L$ or $X_E$, use $F_Y(P)=|P_{\bar x_Y}|$ on finite etale covers. By [thm-galois-lc-etale] the equivalence between finite etale covers and finite locally constant sheaves respects these fibre functors. Thus [def-galois-fibre-functor] identifies $G_Y$ with $\operatorname{Aut}(F_Y)$, with the topology of evaluation on finite-cover fibres. Indeed an isomorphism of objects conjugates their evaluation coordinates by a fixed fibre bijection, and every object on either side of the equivalence is isomorphic to one in its image. The two families of evaluation coordinates therefore induce the same topology; one may throughout choose small skeletons, as in that definition.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: For $E\subseteq E'$ let $t_{E',E}:G_{E'}\to G_E$, and let $r_E:G_L\to G_E$, be the continuous homomorphisms of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. Its bijections $\tau_P$ identify fibres of pullbacks with the original fibres by composing with the first projection. For an iterated pullback these identifications compose: both send a geometric point to its composite with the projections to the original cover. Consequently $t_{E'',E}=t_{E',E}\circ t_{E'',E'}$ and $r_E=t_{E',E}\circ r_{E'}$, since the actions agree on every finite-cover fibre. The map $R:g\mapsto(r_E(g))_E$ therefore takes values in the subgroup $H$ of compatible families from the statement, is a group homomorphism, and is continuous: all its product coordinates are continuous, and $H$ has the subspace topology.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: The map $R$ is injective. Suppose $r_E(g)=1$ for every $E$. For any finite etale $P\to X_L$, clause (1) of [lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent] supplies $P_E\to X_E$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:(P_E)_L\xrightarrow{\sim}P$. Under the fibre bijection of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], $g$ acts on $F_L((P_E)_L)$ as $r_E(g)$ acts on $F_E(P_E)$, hence trivially. Naturality for $\alpha$ makes its action on $F_L(P)$ trivial too. As this holds for every $P$, $g$ is the identity natural automorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: Fix $a=(a_E)_E\in H$. For a finite etale $P\to X_L$, choose $E,P_E,\alpha$ as in descent clause (1). Write $\tau_{E,P_E}:F_L((P_E)_L)\to F_E(P_E)$ for the fibre bijection of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], and put $b=F_L(\alpha)\circ\tau_{E,P_E}^{-1}$. Define the candidate permutation on $F_L(P)$ by $A_P=b\circ(a_E)_{P_E}\circ b^{-1}$. It is a permutation, since each factor is a bijection. This gives actual permutations on the given fibres; their independence of the model and their naturality are verified next.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: Enlarging a chosen model from $E$ to $E'\supseteq E$ does not change $A_P$. Indeed compatibility gives $t_{E',E}(a_{E'})=a_E$. The action identity of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], applied to $P_E$, says that the permutation of $a_{E'}$ on the fibre of $(P_E)_{E'}$ is carried by $\tau$ to $(a_E)_{P_E}$. The fibre bijection $b'$ for the enlarged model is the composite of $b$ with this same $\tau$, by the projection formula checked in step 3. Substituting into $b'(a_{E'})_{(P_E)_{E'}}(b')^{-1}$ gives exactly $b(a_E)_{P_E}b^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: The permutation is independent of all choices. Suppose also $\beta:(Q_{E'})_L\xrightarrow{\sim}P$. Move both models to a common finite field $J$ by step 1; step 6 preserves their candidate permutations. Apply clause (2) of [lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent] to the morphism $\beta^{-1}\alpha:(P_J)_L\to(Q_J)_L$. At some $J'\supseteq J$ it is the pullback of a morphism $u:P_{J'}\to Q_{J'}$. Let $b_P:F_{J'}(P_{J'})\to F_L(P)$ and $b_Q:F_{J'}(Q_{J'})\to F_L(P)$ be the two fibre identifications. The natural fibre bijections of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] give $F_{J'}(u)=b_Q^{-1}b_P$. Naturality of $a_{J'}$ gives $(a_{J'})_{Q_{J'}}F_{J'}(u)=F_{J'}(u)(a_{J'})_{P_{J'}}$. Substitution yields $b_P(a_{J'})_{P_{J'}}b_P^{-1}=b_Q(a_{J'})_{Q_{J'}}b_Q^{-1}$. Only a morphism $u$ is needed: we never assume that the descended morphism is an isomorphism of covers.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: For any morphism $v:P\to Q$ over $X_L$, choose models of both objects at a common field, and use descent clause (2) again to descend the morphism between these models after enlarging the field. Denote it by $v_J:P_J\to Q_J$, with fibre identifications $b_P,b_Q$. Naturality of the pullback-fibre identifications in [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] says $F_L(v)b_P=b_QF_J(v_J)$. The naturality equation for $a_J$ now gives $A_QF_L(v)=F_L(v)A_P$ after multiplying by $b_P^{-1}$ and $b_Q$. Thus $(A_P)_P$ is a natural automorphism $T(a)$ of $F_L$, hence an element of $G_L$ by step 2. Invertibility is objectwise; alternatively the same construction for $(a_E^{-1})_E$ gives its inverse.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: For $P_E$ over $X_E$, compute $T(a)$ on $(P_E)_L$ using that very model and its identity isomorphism. Its action is $\tau_{E,P_E}^{-1}(a_E)_{P_E}\tau_{E,P_E}$; the action characterization of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] therefore gives $r_E(T(a))=a_E$ on every cover fibre. Hence $R(T(a))=a$. For $g\in G_L$, either the same formula gives $T(R(g))_P=g_P$ for every descended model, or injectivity from step 4 gives $T(R(g))=g$. Since $R$ is a homomorphism, it is now a group isomorphism with inverse $T$.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, label lemma-limit, second assertion; explicit fibre-functor argument for the sentence The second statement is formal given the statement on categories

proof.text: Finally $T$ is continuous. For each fixed finite cover $P$ over $X_L$, fix once a model $E,P_E,\alpha$ supplied by descent clause (1). Its evaluation coordinate $a\mapsto T(a)_P$ is the composite $H\to G_E\to\operatorname{Aut}(F_E(P_E))\to\operatorname{Aut}(F_L(P))$. The first map is the product coordinate restricted to $H$, the second is the evaluation map for the topology of [def-galois-fibre-functor], and the last is conjugation by the fixed bijection $b$ of step 5 between finite discrete sets. All are continuous. The evaluation topology of step 2 then makes $T$ continuous. Together with continuity of $R$ in step 3 this proves the asserted topological group isomorphism, with precisely the specified projection components and transition maps.
